title: Add mixed-workload replay runner + standardized p95 tables/plots output
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: For the mixed-workload scheduler prototype we need a repeatable way to (a) replay "customer-like" prompt-length mixes and arrival patterns, and (b) produce consistent, comparable outputs across baseline vs. policy experiments. Today benchmark-lab has good single-scenario runners, but results are inconsistent across scripts and hard to diff at p95/p99, especially when we need breakdowns (queue wait vs service) and a stable "report" artifact for canary readouts.

This PR adds a new mixed-workload replay runner and standardizes the output format (tables + plots) so perf-canary and humans can consume it reliably.

What’s in this PR (high level): Adds a new runner `mixed_replay` that can replay synthetic mixes (config-defined distributions) as well as trace-based mixes (pre-recorded prompt length + inter-arrival patterns). Produces a single structured results bundle per run: `results.json` (canonical), `summary.csv` (flat), `summary.md` (human-readable), and a small set of plots (`latency_cdf.png`, `latency_hist.png`, `queue_wait_breakdown.png`). Adds baseline-vs-candidate comparison mode (two results dirs in, one `comparison.md` out) with focus on p95 tail deltas + throughput regression. Normalizes metric naming for mixed-workload scenarios so downstream dashboards/CI gates don’t need special casing (e.g., `latency_ms_p95_overall`, `latency_ms_p95_short`, `latency_ms_p95_long`, `throughput_rps`, `tokens_per_s`, `gpu_util_pct`, `queue_wait_ms_p95_short`, etc.).

Why: The scheduler prototype is explicitly optimizing tail latency under mixed traffic. We need apples-to-apples reporting that highlights p95 improvements for short/interactive requests while catching throughput regressions and long-queue starvation signals. The existing ad-hoc output makes it too easy to miss a regression or misread a run.

Runner usage: `bench run mixed_replay --scenario scenarios/mixed_workload/mix_70_30.yaml --endpoint http://localhost:8080 --duration 600 --warmup 60 --out results/2024-11-12_mix_70_30_baseline` Trace replay: `bench run mixed_replay --trace traces/customer_like/trace_a.jsonl --endpoint http://localhost:8080 --duration 900 --warmup 60 --out results/trace_a_candidate` Compare: `bench compare --baseline results/trace_a_baseline --candidate results/trace_a_candidate --out results/trace_a_comparison`

Notes on metrics and p95 analysis: The runner records overall and per-class latency distributions (short vs long) based on request tags emitted by the runtime (or classification in the trace file). If the runtime does not emit class tags, we fall back to a deterministic heuristic (prompt_tokens <= threshold) and record that threshold in `results.json` for traceability. We keep the reporting focused on p95/p99 and include a simple tail breakdown plot using available spans/fields: `client_to_enqueue_ms`, `queue_wait_ms`, `prefill_ms`, `decode_ms` when present. If spans aren’t present, the breakdown plot is skipped but the report calls that out explicitly.

Implementation details: New runner lives in `bench/runners/mixed_replay.py`. Added config schema for scenario mixes in `bench/scenarios/mixed_workload/*.yaml` (synthetic distributions and load shapes). Trace format: jsonl with required fields `prompt_tokens`, `max_new_tokens`, `t_ms` (relative send time), optional `class` (short|long), optional `streaming` flag. Output: `bench/reporting/standard_report.py` is a new module that the runner uses; other runners can migrate later but are unchanged for now.

Out of scope: No changes to the Redwood runtime or scheduler in this PR. No attempt to standardize every existing benchmark runner’s outputs—this adds the pathway needed for mixed-workload gating first.

Validation: Ran locally against runtime baseline and scheduler prototype builds; reports generated for 4 scenarios (70/30 mix, 90/10 bursty, trace_a, trace_b). Added unit tests for report formatting and trace parsing; added a lightweight integration test that runs the runner with a fake endpoint and verifies artifact layout.

Follow-ups: (1) Wire `bench compare` output into perf-canary publisher (separate PR in perf-canary repo). (2) Align metric names with runtime instrumentation PR once finalized (expect minor rename only).

conversation: Jonas Weber: Report looks good. Can we make sure p95 deltas are front-and-center in the markdown output? I don’t want folks scrolling through raw percentiles.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep. I’ll move the p95/p99 delta table to the top of `comparison.md` and add an explicit throughput regression line with a default ±3% callout.
Claire Dubois: On trace format: please document required fields and how we interpret `t_ms`. Also, if `class` is missing, we should write the fallback threshold into the results so we can reproduce.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `bench/traces/README.md` with required/optional fields + examples. Also added `classification_fallback` block in `results.json` (threshold + reason).
Sana Farid: I’m worried about plots being too heavy for CI artifacts. Are we generating huge images?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Plots are fixed size (1200x800) PNG and we only emit 3 by default. There’s a `--no-plots` flag if needed. CI artifact-size-check added to keep us honest.
Omar El-Sayed: Metric names: can we align with what runtime instrumentation is landing? I think we’re using `queue_wait_ms_*` whereas runtime may expose `scheduler_queue_wait_ms_*`.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Good call. For now I kept it runner-side and prefixed in the json output under `derived_metrics`. Once runtime metrics names are finalized we can do a single mapping update without changing report consumers.
Jonas Weber: Approved after the markdown re-ordering + throughput callout.
Claire Dubois: Approved (docs + fallback capture addressed).
Sana Farid: Approved (artifact sizing + flag is enough).
release_notes: benchmark-lab: new `mixed_replay` runner to replay mixed prompt-length workloads (synthetic + trace-based)
standardized report artifacts for p95/p99 analysis (json/csv/md + plots) and baseline-vs-candidate comparisons
